# transpiler

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/pkg/transpiler"
```

Package transpiler exposes TGo compilation and expression rewriting.

Compile writes and checks generated Go in the source module. Commands and other tools use the same compiler.

Load and InsertAfter support tools that need statements at an expression's evaluation point. The callback receives evaluated results, not source text that could run the expression again. Source keeps its original checked syntax so callers can apply another rewrite.

Go package types remain visible through Source.Package. Keep this API small; module policy and lowering details belong to internal packages.

## func Compile

```go
func Compile(dir string)
```

Compile translates the module's TGo files into Go files in the same module. Invalid source and compiler failures panic.

## type After

After receives references to the evaluated expression results.

```go
type After = lowering.After
```

## type Site

Site identifies an expression in the original source. Offsets are bytes.

```go
type Site = lowering.Site
```

## type Source

Source contains the original syntax and its type information.

```go
type Source struct {
    Package *packages.Package
    Sites   []Site
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Load

```go
func Load(dir, pattern string) (*Source, error)
```

Load reads one Go package. It does not change its syntax tree.

### func \(\*Source\) InsertAfter

```go
func (s *Source) InsertAfter(site Site, after After) (map[string][]byte, error)
```

InsertAfter builds source files with statements after one expression. The callback uses the expression's evaluated results in source order.
